meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the Cyclohexane Reactor Ver 1 unit
meta.scope: From the TK-100 outlet to the product line at HS-115 (TK-106 / TK-107), the hydrogen loop from XV-105 to the purge to fuel gas, and the utility connections at their valves (cooling water, MP steam, boiler feed water, LP steam export, nitrogen, flare header, instrument air, electrical power).
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: The unit is operated by trained staff at the design conditions. Nitrogen, instrument air and power are available at start-up. Instruments and relief valves are tested on the plan in the maintenance procedure.
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

N1.causes:
Running feed pump P-100A stops (motor trip) and P-100B is not started
FV-101 closes (fails closed on loss of instrument air)
XV-101 closed by the SIS or spuriously
TK-100 empty or suction strainer blocked
N1.cons: Reaction stops: R-101 cools, hydrogen consumption falls and the loop pressure rises until PIC-105 closes PV-105; production lost and a new light-off needed. A pump running against a closed FV-101 or XV-101 overheats and its seal can leak benzene.

N1.dev: More benzene than the hydrogen and heat removal can take
N1.causes:
FIC-101 output driven high (controller or positioner fault, set-point entry error)
FI-101 transmitter reading low
FV-101 trim damaged
N1.cons: Conversion in R-101 falls and unreacted benzene passes to R-102 and R-103, which then release its heat of reaction: R-102 and the adiabatic R-103 bed heat up (about 9 °C per 1 % benzene slip), the product goes off-spec and the bed can run away.

N1.causes:
FV-101 partly stuck
P-100A/B worn or cavitating
suction strainer partly blocked
N1.cons: Lower rate and margin; R-101 runs with more hydrogen excess. No hazard.

N1.dev: Reactor liquid and hydrogen flow back toward P-100A/B and TK-100
N1.causes:
Feed pump stops while R-101 is at 30.0 bar g with FV-101 and XV-101 open
no non-return valve shown on the pump discharge
N1.cons: Hot liquid saturated with hydrogen enters the feed line and the atmospheric tank TK-100: tank overpressure, release of hydrogen and benzene vapour, fire.

N1.dev: Feed line at pump shut-off pressure (dead-headed pump)
N1.causes:
XV-101 closed by the SIS or FV-101 closed while P-100A runs
a manual valve downstream left shut
N1.cons: Pump runs at shut-off: liquid heats, seal and bearing damage, benzene leak at the seal (flammable, carcinogenic).

N1.dev: Benzene feed hotter than the design 40 °C
N1.causes:
TK-100 heated by sun or tracing left on
product recycled to the tank hot
N1.cons: Slightly less heat absorbed by the feed (TIC-101 compensates); pump NPSH margin falls, cavitation.

N1.causes:
Off-spec benzene cargo
TK-100 contaminated
wrong tank lined up
N1.cons: The Raney-Ni in R-101 is poisoned irreversibly: conversion falls, benzene slips to R-102 and R-103 (more heat there), product off-spec; the catalyst must be replaced.

N1.causes:
Tank bottoms drawn into the suction
water not drained from TK-100
N1.cons: Water flashes in R-101 at 200 °C: pressure surge, catalyst activity lost, water carried to V-104 and the product.

sg.text: PIC-105 holds loop pressure by closing PV-105
FIC-101 in AUTO opens FV-101 further
XV-101 closes on any SIS trip
trip procedure stops the feed pump
fresh catalyst through the catalyst pot HV-117
PSHH-101 trips at 33.5 bar g (3 s)

recs.text: Add a high-high benzene flow or benzene-to-hydrogen ratio trip (FI-101 against FI-103) that closes XV-101; the feed can run far above design with no trip.
Add a high-high temperature trip on R-102 with its own element (set below the R-102 boiling point at loop pressure).
Fit a non-return valve on the P-100A/B discharge and close XV-101 when no feed pump runs.
Analyse every benzene receipt for sulphur and water; drain TK-100 water; consider a guard bed ahead of R-101.
Auto-start the standby pumps P-100B, P-101B and P-102B on low discharge pressure or flow.
Write a Raney-Ni handling procedure: always wet and under nitrogen, metered charges through HV-117, filter-cake handling.
Fit minimum-flow bypasses on P-100A/B and P-102A/B.
Add an R-103 bed-rise alarm (TI-107E minus TI-106) as early warning of benzene slip.
